articles.title_orig: ‘A Ticking Time Bomb’: An Economic Crisis Looms in Indonesia
articles.title_zh: ‘A Ticking Time Bomb’: An Economic Crisis Looms in Indonesia
articles.content_orig:
Indonesia's benchmark stock index plunged over 5% on Monday to its lowest level in six years, as concerns over a potential downgrade by MSCI intensified fears of further foreign investor outflows.
The Jakarta Composite Index tumbled to its lowest level since early October 2020, extending a bruising sell-off in Indonesian equities. MSCI, the index provider, on Friday proposed reclassifying Indonesia directly from an emerging market to stand-alone status, raising the prospect of the country's removal from major global equity benchmarks.
MSCI is expected to make a final decision by June, with the potential reclassification hinging on whether Indonesian authorities can demonstrate meaningful improvements in market governance and transparency.
Goldman Sachs warned in a Sunday note that a full removal from MSCI's emerging-market indexes could trigger approximately $5.6 billion in passive fund outflows, equivalent to 18 days of average daily trading volume for constituents of the MSCI Indonesia Investable Market Index.
An additional $2.7 billion could be at risk if FTSE Russell subsequently takes similar action, although the bank stressed that such a move would be a separate scenario.
Goldman estimated that active funds benchmarked to MSCI and FTSE indexes hold more than $8 billion in Indonesian equities, although any selling by these investors would be discretionary rather than automatically triggered by a downgrade.
The bank maintained its underweight rating on Indonesian equities, citing persistent index uncertainty, weak corporate earnings and macroeconomic headwinds.
"Valuations have compressed significantly, but remain above historical troughs; index, earnings, and macro risks constrain a re-rating," Goldman strategists led by Alvin So wrote.
The MSCI Indonesia Index has fallen 47% this year as of Friday, data provided by the bank showed, with foreign investors withdrawing a net $5.1 billion from Indonesian equities over the period.
Foreign ownership of Indonesian stocks has declined to 25% in October from 27% in January, while the value of foreign holdings has nearly halved to approximately $130 billion from $250 billion, the bank said.
Despite the steep declines, Goldman cautioned that Indonesian equities may not have bottomed. The MSCI Indonesia Index's 12-month forward price-to-earnings ratio has fallen to 7.3 times, its lowest level since the global financial crisis, but remains above historical troughs.
The strategists also expect Indonesia's central bank to raise interest rates twice more, by 25 basis points each in the fourth quarter of 2026 and first quarter of 2027, potentially adding further pressure to economic growth and equity valuations.

articles.title_orig: Meet the researchers leaving the US because of Trump's funding cuts and politicization of science
articles.title_zh: Meet the researchers leaving the US because of Trump's funding cuts and politicization of science
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in

Halley Froehlich never expected to leave the United States, where her family lineage stretches back to the 1700s, to pursue her scientific career.
Yet, faced with stalled federal grants and growing uncertainty over the country's research environment, she packed her life into boxes and relocated to Finland alongside her husband and daughter. She now studies how climate change affects edible fish, shellfish, and seaweed at the University of Helsinki .
Her departure reflects a wider trend. When the Trump administration began reshaping the American scientific sector last year by altering the federal grant distribution process and seeking greater political influence over funded projects, foreign academic institutions recognized an opportunity.
Many introduced dedicated schemes designed to entice U.S.-based scholars by offering stable financial support and academic freedom.
A growing number of academics have accepted these international offers. Though comprehensive nationwide data remains difficult to aggregate, university officials, researchers, and professional associations describe the ongoing shift as clear, unprecedented, and concerning.
"You can almost talk to any vice president for research at a university and they will tell you of one or two top faculty that they’ve lost," said Tobin Smith, senior vice president of government relations and public policy for the Association of American Universities.
White House spokesperson Liz Huston said Trump is "ending waste" and is "committed to keeping America the world leader in scientific innovation, and that means funding real science."
Despite those assurances, an April report from the Business for Federal Research Funding Coalition revealed that more than half of U.S. states have lost scientists to recruitment programs in other countries.
Survey data from last March indicated that early-career biomedical scientists were about 20 percentage points less likely to say they wanted to stay in the U.S. "now" than they did six months earlier.
Furthermore, figures from the American Institute of Physics show that physics Ph.D. graduates in 2025 departed the U.S. at the highest rate observed in 30 years.
Institutions in nations such as Canada , France , Belgium , and Finland are publicly advertising their success in drawing scholars from U.S. organizations. For a country that far and away leads the world in Nobel prizes for medicine, physics, and chemistry, researchers view this as a disturbing and surprising development.
"It used to be the shining city on the hill where we all want to go," said Christine Stawitz, now at the University of Birmingham in England . "That reputational loss, I think, is hard to quantify, but also really damaging."
Stawitz stepped down from her job at the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration last year to become a research software engineer in the United Kingdom .
She noted that NOAA no longer aligned with her values, particularly after receiving directives to strip websites of references to climate change and diversity, equity and inclusion topics.
She added that the state of American science has become a recurring topic of conversation at international gatherings. " People talk about the U.S. at conferences in the U.K. now like, I don't know what's going on there. It's not good," she said.
For Froehlich, the choice to relocate developed over time. Already concerned by issues surrounding school safety and gun violence in the U.S., she watched as the national research landscape was overturned.
At the University of California, Santa Barbara, grant postponements and cancellations left colleagues struggling and student researchers in tears. Doubts regarding future federal backing for her climate-focused research mounted.
"The cumulative effect of those things ultimately ended up making us really serious about, I don’t think here is our home anymore," said Froehlich.
She ultimately accepted an offer through an initiative by the Research Council of Finland, securing five years of guaranteed funding totaling about $3 million. She moved into a flat by the Baltic Sea in Helsinki and is taking university-sponsored Finnish lessons.
Foreign researchers who were drawn to the U.S. for its reputation as a global leader in science are also seeking different places to do their work.
Married biologists James Letts, who is Canadian, and Maria Maldonado, who is Argentinian, left their academic positions at the University of California, Davis to join Australia 's Monash University. Both earned their doctoral degrees in New York and spent over a decade doing science in the U.S.
Grant-related uncertainty—including laying off a staff scientist while waiting for stalled funding—motivated them to make the move.
"All I want to do is do great science and make discoveries, but I want my work to mean something as well. And the opportunity to do that seemed very difficult in the U.S.," Letts said.
Immigrants have historically won 40 percent of the U.S. science Nobel Prizes. However, Omar Yaghi, a 2025 Nobel Prize winner for chemistry, departed his position at the University of California, Berkeley this year to direct an artificial intelligence lab at China’s Tsinghua University.
The U.S. remains a science powerhouse, full of institutions with robust research communities and well-resourced facilities that attract foreign talent.
Even if every European country threw open its doors, there still would not be enough capacity to accommodate every American scientist. Many researchers are choosing to stay, searching for new sources of funding or pivoting to industry positions.
Nevertheless, concerns persist regarding the ongoing erosion of reputation and talent. The Trump administration has cut or frozen up to $174 billion in federal grants since the president's second term began, according to tracking data compiled by the States United Democracy Center and Grant Witness.
Additionally, a proposed rule from the Office of Management and Budget could accord political appointees more control over which future projects are funded, though a resolution approved by Congress has delayed a final decision on the rule until December.
Scientists who have moved away and those remaining in the U.S. are worried about what lies ahead. They warn that the next generation of scientists may face fewer graduate programs, diminished funding, and reduced mentorship—effects that could take a decade or longer for the U.S. scientific enterprise to fully feel.
Major research institutions accepted 15% fewer applicants for fall 2026 doctoral programs compared to last year, according to admissions data collected by the Association of American Universities. One of the impacted students was a mentee of Smith's.
"What is one of my pieces of advice to that young man? Next year, look in Canada," he said.

articles.title_orig: Weil Is Engaged in Merger Talks, Leadership Tells Partners
articles.title_zh: Weil Is Engaged in Merger Talks, Leadership Tells Partners
articles.content_orig:
Weil Gotshal & Manges is pursuing a merger with another law firm and is in discussions to secure the tie-up, its leaders have told top partners.
Weilâs leadership told certain practice group chiefs the firm is negotiating a memorandum of understanding detailing the merger with the unnamed firm, according to two people familiar with the situation. A broader announcement could happen as early as this week, they said, though they cautioned that nothing could come of the talks.
Weil has seen a string of departures both in the US and London this year, weakening its corporate department and fueling rampant merger speculation. Spokespeople for the firm did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The three partners leading Weil are current executive partner Barry Wolf, his successor Ramona Nee, and managing partner Jonathon Soler.
The merger talks come as Weil prepared for more departures, including the exit of its former corporate department co-managing partner Michael Hickey, who is expected to join Sullivan & Cromwell. Other practice group leaders have been in discussions to join rivals, according to multiple sources.
Hickey did not respond to a request for comment.
Law firm merger negotiations are inherently delicate and can be affected by partner departures as the talks drag on. Confidentiality is also often viewed as a crucial aspect of successful mergers.
Weil was said to be considering merger negotiations shortly after its powerful corporate department chair Michael Aiello in September announced he would leave for Cravath, Swaine & Moore. Sources familiar with the firm voiced support for the idea in the wake of his exit.
Aielloâs departure came after a handful of partners left for Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison and Simpson Thacher & Bartlett, two rival firms that over the past decade have zoomed past Weil on key financial metrics.
Partner exits have also hit Weilâs London office, including the defection of key M&A partner David Avery-Gee to Sullivan & Cromwell and London finance head Tom Richardsâ pending jump to Simpson Thacher. The firm last month rehired Debra Sinclair, who left for Willkie Farr & Gallagher a decade ago, and private equity veteran Peter Feist from Cravath.

articles.title_zh: Elon Musk Says He Will Give a SpaceX Share to ‘Every Kid in America’
articles.content_orig:
SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, the world's richest person, pledged Monday to give each child in the U.S. one of his SpaceX shares.
Elon Musk has pledged to give every child in America one share of SpaceX next year, signaling that the planned giveaway could be the first of several.
"Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many," he wrote in a Monday post on X.
The pledge followed an exchange with artificial intelligence company Anthropic over its plans to dedicate a portion of its equity to public benefit initiatives.
TESLA'S NEW ROADSTER MAKES A FLYING DEBUT, HITTING 60 MPH IN UNDER A SECOND
Elon Musk speaks during the World Economic Forum (WEF) annual meeting in Davos on January 22, 2026. (Fabrice COFFRINI / AFP via Getty Images / Getty Images)
On Sunday, Musk urged Anthropic to distribute shares directly to the public after the company outlined its plans for the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund.
Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk receives the National Medal of Science from U.S. President Donald Trump during the Golden Age of American Innovation Summit at the Institute of Peace on Oct. 8, 2026, in Washington, D.C. ( Win McNamee/Getty Images / Getty Images)
"We’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity dedicated entirely to the public benefit. It will start off with 5% of our shares. For every 50% increase in the company’s value over a set baseline, we can contribute up to an extra 2%, subject to our board’s discretion. In total, this means that roughly 20% of Anthropic’s shares are committed to the public good," Anthropic noted in a Sunday post on X.
"Our co-founders have already pledged to donate 80% of their equity, and around half our employees are donating a portion of their equity as part of a donation matching program we’ve run since our founding," the company added.
Anthropic Co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei arrives at the Eisenhower Executive Office Building on Sept. 29, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Finn Gomez/Getty Images / Getty Images)
Responding to Anthropic's announcement, Musk wrote, "I recommend giving the shares directly to the public."
He then indicated that he intended to follow that approach himself.
"This is what I will be doing," he added in another post.

By Caroline Valetkevitch and Danilo Masoni
NEW YORK/MILAN, Oct 19 (Reuters) - The Nasdaq rose more than 1% on Monday as tech shares rebounded ahead of a big week for AI-related earnings, while European stocks and the euro fell as unrest in France added to concerns about the country's fiscal outlook.
French bonds and Paris-listed ‌stocks also fell as the widespread protests across France underscored the difficulties the government faces in reducing its large deficit.
France's central government asked some local authorities to ‌impose curfews as it faced pressure over security failings on Monday, after looting stemming from the protests.
Tech stocks on Wall Street recovered some ground after a bruising week, with an index of semiconductors up 1.6%. On Friday, the index ​sank in its eighth straight day of declines, its longest losing streak since 2008.
With results due from Meta on Wednesday, and results from Tesla and chipmakers Lam Research and Texas Instruments also due this week, investors will be watching for signs that massive AI spending ultimately pays off.
"Investors are buying the correction dip that we had," said Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at Spartan Capital Securities in New York.
"The market is now going to go through a very critical test over the next two weeks. We have some big-name earnings coming out," he said. "In terms of technology, the test ‌of whether or not the spending on AI... will be met ⁠with satisfaction is going to be critical."
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 36.38 points, or 0.07%, to 51,966.03, the S&P 500 rose 31.29 points, or 0.41%, to 7,690.73 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 290.85 points, or 1.11%, to 26,430.89. MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe rose 0.88 points, ⁠or 0.08%, to 1,129.98.
Meta is one of five AI hyperscalers expected to increase combined capital expenditure to about $1.2 trillion next year, according to Goldman Sachs.
Results from SpaceX are also due on Tuesday. Overall, US earnings are still expected to rise about 30%, largely driven by growth in the technology sector.
US Treasury yields rose on Monday, with the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield coming off its biggest weekly drop in seven ​months, ​as concerns about the impact of higher interest rates on AI stocks abated. The yield on the benchmark ​US 10-year Treasury note was up 4.2 basis points at 5.14%.
The recent ‌bond selloff had also intensified scrutiny of the AI sector's massive funding needs.
In economic data, the National Association of Home Builders/Wells Fargo Housing Market index on Monday showed a drop of three points to 29 this month, the lowest level since June 2012 and below the 31 estimate of economists polled by Reuters.
Recent comments from Federal Reserve officials, including Chair Kevin Warsh, suggest policymakers are in no rush to hike rates again. On Friday, Warsh expressed optimism about US economic strength but gave no indication of whether or when more hikes will be needed.
EUROPEAN STOCKS, EURO FALL
The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.8%, while France's blue-chip CAC 40 index dropped 1.1%.
France's 10-year yield earlier was up 13 basis points to 4.9% while the German 10-year yield, the ‌benchmark for the euro zone, was also higher. The spread between French OATs and safe-haven German Bunds ​has widened to 147 basis points, trading at levels last seen during the 2011 to 2012 European debt crisis, ​from around 110 bps in late September.
Widespread weekend unrest in the euro zone's second-largest ​economy underscored the challenge facing the French government as it seeks to reduce its large budget deficit ahead of next year's presidential elections.
The euro ‌fell 0.24% to $1.1212.
The US dollar was boosted by the rebound in tech ​stocks. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against ​a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, rose 0.17% to 101.97.
Meanwhile, the Australian dollar rose 0.49% versus the greenback after data showed China's economic growth rebounded from three-year lows, expanding at a 4.5% annual pace in the third quarter.
Oil prices were mixed, with investors digesting attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on a Yemeni military training ​camp and renewed attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military facilities.
Brent ‌crude futures fell 31 cents to settle at $109.55 a barrel. Brent fell more than $3 earlier in the session.
US West Texas Intermediate gained $2.25 to $103.66 a barrel, the highest ​settlement since September 15.
Spot gold fell 0.61% to $4,139.67 an ounce.
(Reporting by Caroline Valetkevitch in New York and Danilo Masoni in Milan; additional reporting by Wayne Cole ​and Avinash P; Editing by Stephen Coates, Kevin Buckland, Xevi Fontdegloria, Nick Zieminski and Deepa Babington)

articles.title_orig: Stock Market Today: S&P 500 and Nasdaq close higher as tech stocks surged, but the Dow slips as yields rise
articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: S&P 500 and Nasdaq close higher as tech stocks surged, but the Dow slips as yields rise
articles.content_orig:
Hello, this is Hui Jie writing to you from Singapore. Welcome to another edition of CNBC's Daily Open.
After a bruising week for the tech trade, investors seem to have came back into the sector, with the Nasdaq Composite rallying overnight.
The optimism is cautious, with debt concerns still a key worry for a sector that has seen record bond issuance this year.
Investors are once again piling into tech, after fears over AI financing, rising competition and possible excess chip supply in a few years drove them to cash out of the market last week.
The Nasdaq Composite rebounded more than 1% on Monday, after sliding 4.5% last week and snapping a four-week winning streak.
Intel advanced 2% after JPMorgan analysts upgraded their rating on the chipmaker. Advanced Micro Devices added 1.8%, and Micron Technology jumped about 3%.
It was not a wholesale embrace of the sector, however. Funding concerns still loom, especially over neocloud companies.
Shares of neocloud mainstay CoreWeave reversed course from earlier gains, falling 0.4%, even after receiving Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to buy from neutral.
CoreWeave shares plunged more than 25% last week — their biggest one-week drop since November 2025 — over debt concerns.
Another company that is also facing credit stress is Oracle . It risks a credit rating downgrade that could tip its debt into junk territory. Oracle's rating at S&P Credit Ratings is BBB-, the lowest level in the investment-grade spectrum.
While the bonds are still investment grade, the shift in sentiment can be seen in the spread of Oracle's five-year credit default swaps, which are insurance against default.
Oracle's five-year CDS spread, or premium, is currently at 295 basis points, after briefly hitting 300 basis points on Thursday. It is up 287% in one year.
The range is more in line with BB and B credit, which is high yield, said Gavan Nolan, executive director of fixed income pricing at S&P Global Market Intelligence.
When the year started, investors were predicting a slew of AI companies going public , including SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI.
But now investors will have to settle for less , with OpenAI ruling out its market debut in 2026 and several other planned offerings postponed this year .
On prediction market platform Kalshi , speculators think the only major company left that might officially announce an IPO this year is Anthropic, which confidentially filed a prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission in early June.
Only Anthropic offers greater than 50% odds — 75% as of Monday morning — to officially announce an IPO this year, out of the 23 companies that Kalshi lists on its market that remain open to trade.
On the geopolitical front, the tensions between Washington and Kyiv continue to rise with President Donald Trump saying Monday he would meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping to discuss how to end the Ukraine war.
That comes after the Wall Street Journal reported that Putin in an Oct. 9 phone call with Trump had floated the idea of a trilateral summit with Xi next month, although the meeting is envisioned to exclude Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
"Anything I can do to end the war, whether somebody's there or not," Trump told reporters when asked about the potential meeting as he departed the White House for a campaign rally in Kansas.
Trump also doubled down on his criticism of the Ukrainian leader when he was asked about Zelenskyy's remarks that Trump is on the wrong side of history , saying that "Zelenskyy doesn't know what he's talking about," and reiterating his call for Kyiv to "get a new president."
Elon Musk says he’ll give a SpaceX share to every child in America next year
SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said Monday that he'll give every child in the U.S. one of his shares in the company next year.
Musk currently owns about 4.8 billion SpaceX shares, according to an August SEC filing. That figure rises to 6.4 billion when taking into account unvested awards and stock options, representing a 48.4% beneficial stake in the company.
There were 72 million children under 18 in the U.S. as of July 1, 2025, according to official census data.
That would amount to the CEO giving away about $10.5 billion worth of shares, taking into account SpaceX's closing stock price of $146.03 as of Friday.
— Kai Nicol-Schwarz, Lora Kolodny

articles.title_orig: United Airlines CEO says US should have an inheritance tax 'close to 100%' and he'd pay it
articles.title_zh: United Airlines CEO says US should have an inheritance tax 'close to 100%' and he'd pay it
articles.content_orig:
Dagen McDowell slams United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby over his proposal for a national wealth tax and a near-100% inheritance tax. She calls out the double taxation and points to the hypocrisy of the airline's own elite status pricing.
United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby is calling for a national wealth tax and inheritance taxes approaching 100% for certain estates, arguing that growing wealth inequality poses a threat to American society.
Kirby, who took home about $32.3 million in total compensation in fiscal year 2025, made the remarks when asked about declining public trust in corporate executives during an interview with The New York Times.
"Wealth inequality has become a danger to our society, and we need to address that," Kirby told the outlet in an interview published Sunday.
United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby is calling for a national wealth tax and inheritance taxes approaching 100% for certain estates. (Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
The airline executive argued that a wealth tax would need to be implemented nationwide rather than at the state level to prevent wealthy Americans from relocating to avoid paying it.
"We should have a national wealth tax — it won’t work by state because people will just move," Kirby told the outlet. "And I think we should have inheritance taxes that get close to 100 percent at some level. I would pay them."
TSA SCALES BACK AIRPORT GATE ACCESS PROGRAM FOR NON-PASSENGERS
Kirby did not specify what wealth threshold would trigger the proposed inheritance tax or what rate he would support for a national wealth tax in the remarks cited.
His comments come as proposals to increase taxes on wealthy Americans continue to generate debate over their potential effects on investment, economic growth and government revenue.
United CEO Scott Kirby also said charging passengers for the services and products they choose allows airlines to serve customers with different preferences. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images)
A federal wealth tax would differ from existing income and estate taxes by targeting the value of an individual's assets rather than solely income or wealth transferred after death.
Kirby's proposal would also represent a significant departure from the current federal estate tax system, which imposes a top marginal rate of 40% on taxable estates above applicable exemptions. The federal estate tax has a basic exemption of $15 million per individual in 2026, according to the IRS .
The United CEO also discussed airline pricing during the Times interview, defending the practice of charging passengers more for certain seating options after being asked about the cost for travelers without frequent-flier status to avoid middle seats.
A United Airlines plane flies past clouds after taking off from San Francisco International Airport. (Tayfun Coskun/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images)
"There are some customers who want to sit in a window seat or a better seat, and that costs money to deliver," Kirby said, according to the Times.
He said charging passengers for the services and products they choose allows airlines to serve customers with different preferences.
CLICK HERE TO GET FOX BUSINESS ON THE GO
Despite his concerns about wealth inequality, Kirby expressed optimism about the broader U.S. economy , telling the newspaper that he believes the country's future is "incredibly bright."

articles.title_orig: Trudy’s moisture will trigger a flood risk from California to Colorado
articles.title_zh: Trudy’s moisture will trigger a flood risk from California to Colorado
articles.content_orig:
Hurricane Trudy will bring flood threat to the Southwest US
Trudy is off the Mexican coast, but its moisture will pour into the southwestern U.S. and will help fuel a multiday flood risk across seven states this week from California to Colorado.
A dip in the jet stream will also funnel in moisture from the Pacific as a strong low-pressure system moves into the region.
Wednesday: The highest risk of flooding on Wednesday covers much of Arizona and parts of New Mexico, as well as southern portions of Colorado and Utah.
There will be an abundance of moisture available to support heavy downpours and training storms. This means storms will produce heavy rain over the same areas for long periods of time. The Weather Prediction Center is forecasting rainfall rates as high as 2 inches per hour.
Some of the biggest concern will be the possibility of mudslides over recent burn scar areas as well as slow canyons and arroyos.
If you have plans to visit any of the national parks in the West this week, make sure you check the forecast daily and pay attention to any warnings or advisories issued.
Set The Weather Company as a 'Preferred Source' to get quicker access to the news you value.
There is also a slight threat of severe weather on Wednesday for portions of Arizona and western New Mexico. Isolated strong wind and hail are the main threats, but a brief tornado is also possible.
Thursday: Moisture will continue to pump into the Southwest on Thursday, only enhancing the flood threat on already saturated soils.
Some forecast models are alluding to near record levels of moisture available for October in this region, which means there’s a great concern for flooding and the possibility that rainfall amounts could end up higher than currently forecast.
While the greatest risk for flooding moves out of California, it remains for much of Arizona, Nevada, New Mexico, Colorado and Utah. This includes places like Las Vegas, Phoenix, Tucson and Albuquerque.
Right now, we are expecting as much as 3 inches of rain across portions of the Desert Southwest, which is more than enough for flash flooding in this region. Some isolated locations could see up to 5 inches.
And yes, we could even squeeze some snow out of this system for some of the higher elevations.
Parts of the Sierra and Rockies could see the first significant snow of the season. This could be a nice base for some of the ski resorts that were robbed of snow last winter.
While widespread snowfall totals will stay under 6 inches, we could see isolated peaks pick up a foot of snow.
Make sure you check back often, as the forecast could change. And don’t be caught off-guard if you are traveling through some of the higher elevations, as the rain could change to snow quickly.

Drivers to get new rights to challenge unfair private parking charges, alongside crack down on car dealers winding back mileages
Drivers will get new rights to challenge unfair private parking charges under new rules announced today. This includes a guaranteed 5 minutes to decide whether to park and 10 minutes to leave once their session ends, and the right to have charges cancelled on appeal for issues they can’t control.
Under the new Private Parking Code of Practice laid in Parliament today (20 October), charges will be scrapped on appeal for honest mistakes, like stopping briefly to check directions, and for situations like a medical emergency, breakdown or broken ticket machine.
For smaller slip-ups, like forgetting a parking permit, entering the wrong vehicle’s registration or forgetting to confirm it in the machine when parking, drivers will face a maximum charge of £20 on appeal.
The Code also freezes the maximum parking charge at £100. Operators who don’t comply risk losing access to DVLA data, meaning that even if they issue a charge, it will be far more difficult to identify the registered owner to pursue payment.
In addition, unscrupulous second-hand car dealers who wind back odometers to disguise a vehicle’s true mileage will also face tougher action. Known as car clocking, fraudulently selling a clocked car is already illegal, but adding it to the official list of banned practices will make it easier for enforcers to crack down, protecting buyers and backing honest businesses.
These changes are the latest measures in the Prime Minister’s series of everyday fixes, tackling the frustrations that cost people time and money to give families more room to breathe.
Today’s action follows moves to stop unfair airline charges, tackle subscription traps, rogue traders, and rip-off school uniform costs.
Being a few minutes late back to your car or typing one digit of your numberplate wrong shouldn’t end with a hefty fine landing on your doormat.
These charges leave people feeling ripped off and out of pocket, so I’m putting a stop to them.
We are introducing clearer rules, longer grace periods and lower charges for genuine mistakes, while going after the deliberate scams that rip drivers off.
Parking should be straightforward, not another everyday hassle. These changes mean drivers get a fairer deal, protected time to park and leave without fear of being unfairly charged, and confidence that private parking providers are held to a higher standard.
It’s yet another step forward in this government’s plan to take the stress out of everyday life and ease the pressure on people’s pockets.
Nobody works hard for their money just to be deceived by a dodgy trader, and this is exactly the kind of everyday rip-off this government is going after.
By making it easier to take action against car clocking, we are protecting consumers’ hard-earned money and supporting businesses that play by the rules.
The government has also promised today to go further still, by consulting as soon as possible next year on private parking debt recovery fees, including on whether to cut an existing £70 cap or scrap the fees altogether.
Data shows just under 17 million private parking charges were issued in the UK last year. In 2025, the government set out proposals to improve standards by consulting on a new Private Parking Code of Practice.
Today’s response sets out the measures being brought in to protect motorists. Parliament will now have time to scrutinise the new Code, before ministers press ahead to bring it into force as soon as possible.
This Code brings in, for the first time, a fully independent Scrutiny and Oversight Board, and requires operators to share more information with government, giving drivers stronger protections than ever before.
Since taking office, the government has also launched a review of airport drop-off charges, cut VAT on electricity bills this winter, frozen fuel duty and rail fares, and raised the Minimum Wage, as it continues to take action to ease the cost of living.
The code will apply in England, Scotland and Wales.
Motorists will have their parking charge cancelled where they can provide evidence that one of the scenarios set out in the Appeals Charter applies to them.
Operators will have to report data on the charges they issue and how appeals are handled, to help raise standards across the industry. This will be scrutinised by a new independent Scrutiny and Oversight Board, giving drivers confidence that the Code is working as intended. The process to set the board up will commence once the code comes into force.
The changes follow a public consultation that ran from July to September 2025 and received 4,526 responses from the public and industry. Motorists were clear that they wanted fairer appeals, and independent oversight of the private parking industry.
The government intends to consult further on the remaining CMA recommendations post-publication of the Code.

articles.title_orig: GLP-1 injections recalled nationwide. See affected products
articles.title_zh: GLP-1 injections recalled nationwide. See affected products
articles.content_orig:
How to Live Better, Longer
Federal inspectors who spent six days inside a Houston compounding pharmacy in August documented 14 problems with how it made sterile injectable drugs, including compounded GLP-1 weight-loss shots , according to an FDA inspection report . The pharmacy, Houston RX LLC, later recalled 64 vials of compounded tirzepatide with niacinamide because of a lack of assurance of sterility.
The findings matter to anyone who buys compounded semaglutide or tirzepatide through a telehealth program, clinic, or med spa. Injectable drugs bypass the skin's natural barrier, so a contaminated vial can cause infection at the injection site or, less often, in the bloodstream. Patients usually cannot tell a safe vial from a compromised one by looking at it. Equipment that has not been depyrogenated, a process that removes fever-causing bacterial residues called endotoxins, can leave those residues behind even when no live germs remain.
The report, known as a Form 483, lists observations made during an inspection. The document states that these observations do not represent a final FDA determination about compliance, and the company can respond or correct them. MedicalDaily could not locate a public response from Houston RX.
Investigators inspected the pharmacy on Vantage Parkway East on six days between August 20 and August 28 and issued the report on the final day. The first observation is blunt: "Personnel performed aseptic manipulations with exposed hair or skin." Inspectors wrote that an operator working inside the ISO 5 hood, the cleanest workspace, had exposed skin on her forehead while stoppering freshly filled semaglutide-niacinamide vials.
Other observations describe the cleanroom air. Pressure readings from July 10 to August 21 between the buffer room and the less clean anteroom were all negative, a reversal that can let dirtier air drift toward sterile work. The report says lots made during that period were released.
Inspectors also wrote that on August 3 the pharmacy recovered microbial growth in the ISO 5 hood after filling a lot of tirzepatide-niacinamide. No investigation followed because the firm's action level was not appropriate, according to the FDA, and that lot was released and partially distributed.
The report adds that staff pressed stoppers into vials by hand, that vials were finished outside the clean area, and that beakers, stir bars and graduated cylinders used for sterile drugs were not sterilized or depyrogenated. A ceiling vent just outside the cleanroom had water stains and what appeared to be mold. On one inspection day, it was dripping condensate near the area where items headed into the cleanroom were wiped down.
Ingredients were another concern. Certificates for the tirzepatide and semaglutide active ingredients were marked for research and development only, as were certificates for other ingredients, and a sermorelin ingredient was labeled for scientific research use. The niacinamide used in all of the pharmacy's GLP-1 formulas met a dietary supplement standard rather than a pharmaceutical one, and several ingredients were not stored at their labeled temperatures.
According to FDA enforcement records summarized in the nonprofit MedShadow Foundation's roundup of recent compounded GLP-1 drug recalls , Houston RX began recalling 64 two-milliliter vials of tirzepatide-niacinamide 20 mg/2 mg per mL on September 25. The FDA classified it as a Class II recall, meaning use may cause temporary or medically reversible health problems, or that serious harm is unlikely. The pharmacy also recalled seven vials of compounded sermorelin, a growth hormone-releasing peptide, citing a lack of process control.
Recall details are posted in the FDA's weekly Enforcement Report database . Patients who use compounded tirzepatide should check the pharmacy name on the label or ask the prescriber which pharmacy filled the order.
Signs of a possible injection-site infection include spreading redness, warmth, swelling, pus or pain that gets worse. Fever, chills, a racing heart, or confusion after an injection can signal a more serious infection and need urgent care. Patients should not stop a prescribed treatment without talking with a clinician, but they can ask for a replacement from a different source.
Side effects and product concerns can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch program , and patients can keep the vial and packaging until they speak with a pharmacist.
Cost drives much of the demand. An October price survey by NexLife, a telehealth company that sells compounded GLP-1s, found a median all-in price of $222 a month for compounded tirzepatide across 14 online programs and $175 for compounded semaglutide across 16, according to its release on GlobeNewswire . Those figures were compiled by the company and have not been independently verified.
The trade-off is oversight. Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved, and the agency's page on unapproved GLP-1 drugs reports 990 adverse event reports tied to compounded semaglutide and more than 730 tied to compounded tirzepatide as of May 31, 2026. The FDA says adverse events from compounded versions are likely underreported, though the reports alone do not prove the drugs caused the problems.
Houston RX is not the only pharmacy with recent sterility-related recalls. The same MedShadow roundup lists recalls of compounded GLP-1 products by Carolina Infusion in Ridgeland, South Carolina, and Apothecary Pharma in Cary, North Carolina.
Patients using compounded products can ask whether the pharmacy is licensed in their state, whether it has recent FDA inspection findings, and whether an FDA-approved version is covered by their insurance. Any further FDA action, such as a warning letter, would depend on the agency's review. For now, the recall notice and inspection report are the clearest public record of what inspectors found.
What did the FDA find at Houston RX?
An August inspection produced a Form 483 listing 14 observations, including exposed skin during sterile work, reversed cleanroom air pressure, microbial growth in a clean hood, unsterilized equipment, possible mold near the cleanroom, and research-grade ingredients.
Which products were recalled?
Houston RX recalled 64 vials of compounded tirzepatide-niacinamide 20 mg/2 mg per mL due to a lack of assurance of sterility and seven vials of compounded sermorelin due to a lack of process control. Both are Class II recalls.
How can I tell if my vial is affected?
Check the pharmacy name on the label and compare it with the FDA Enforcement Report. If you are unsure, ask your prescriber or the dispensing pharmacy.
No illnesses linked to the recalled vials have been publicly reported. The FDA has received more than 1,700 adverse event reports involving compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide overall, but those reports do not establish cause.
What symptoms should I watch for after an injection?
Watch for spreading redness, swelling, warmth, pus, or worsening pain at the injection site. Fever, chills, a fast heartbeat, or confusion need urgent medical care.
Should I stop my GLP-1 treatment?
Do not stop a prescribed medication on your own. Contact your prescriber to discuss a replacement from another pharmacy or an FDA-approved option.

articles.title_orig: Four AI Agents Have Slain Minecraft’s Ender Dragon
articles.title_zh: Four AI Agents Have Slain Minecraft’s Ender Dragon
articles.content_orig:
Agents split up tasks, warned about threats and even recovered items from dead teammates.
Google's Deepmind "AlphaGo" AI is famous for winning at Go , but the company's latest Gemini AI just mastered a far more complex game. Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft's final " Ender Dragon" foe with no human intervention by working individually while sharing tips, threats and mistakes, Google researchers revealed in a new paper . The experiment shows how general agentic AI models can now beat complex games, a feat that used to required custom AI software.
To tackle Minecraft, the Gemini 4 team set four AI agents into a sandboxed, randomized Minecraft survival world with a goal to defeat the Ender Dragon. No roles, strategies or game-specific tools were assigned. Each agent controlled a player using the open-source Mineflayer library and coordinated with teammates through in-game chat and shared memory.
During gameplay, agents quickly elected to split up tasks. They warned each about threats, gave lessons and tips, provided coordinates and even recovered items from dead teammates. Each settled into roles: for example, "janesick" made tools, "gyldenia" gathered food and supplies, "auratian" lit a key portal and "bulicame" built Enderman shelters and landed the final blow.
All told, the process took 27.23 hours, with the majority of time spent on the Ender Dragon. "The four agents wrote and ran 2,783 programs, exchanged 229 messages and died 605 times along the way," the team said. A fifth agent called "the Observer" monitored the session as an independent witness, both to check for cheating and to publish live and summary reports. The agents used 1.35 billion input tokens and the final cost was $810 at Gemini's list price or $1,620 at the standard price.
"To our knowledge, this is the first end-to-end autonomous completion of Minecraft by AI agents, achieved using only the standard Mineflayer library without pre-scouted seeds or other game-specific tools written by humans," the team wrote. "Winning required the agents to keep a coherent plan across thousands of dependent steps for more than a day."

articles.title_zh: Eye-Popping Total Trump Wants to Cash Out of White House Is Exposed
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump has a major goal in mind to achieve before the end of his term, but it has nothing to do with policy.
Trump, 80, has always wanted to financially enrich himself above all else, his longtime biographer Michael Wolff said in the latest installment of his Substack, Howl .
But White House insiders have told him that the alleged total the president seeks is beyond any reasonable expectation.
âThe number people in the White House say, with due consideration and resigned acceptanceâTrump is Trump, after allâthat he wants to reach is $20 billion,â Wolff wrote. âAnd heâd probably like to put in place deals that, when he returns to Mar-a-Lago, can generate for the Trump family $100 million.â
Trump has made more than $2 billion during his second presidential term.
ANDREW CABALLERO-REYNOLDS/AFP via Getty Images
Wolff noted that Trump has already made, by many estimates, billions during his second administration.
The presidentâs financial disclosure , released in late June, revealed that he personally earned more than $1.4 billion in 2025 from cryptocurrency ventures alone.
Trump's wife Melania also launched her own memecoin, which failed miserably.
This included over $635 million in licensing fees from âCelebration Coinsâ and more than $525 million in proceeds from token sales by World Liberty Financialâthe cryptocurrency firm he founded with his sons.
By clicking â SUBSCRIBE â you agree to our Terms of Use and Privacy Policy .
A New York Times analysis gauged that Trump had âpulled in at least $2.2 billionâ in 2025, while Forbes estimated in September that he had become âan estimated $2.7 billion richer than when he won the 2024 election.â
Trumpâs love of money, Wolff writes, is what drives his relationship with Russian dictator Vladimir Putin.
Late Friday, the president defied previous geopolitical strategy to waive sanctions on Russian oil, which many viewed as him cozying up to the oligarch .
Trump's infatuation with his dictator pal is no secret.
Andrew Harnik/Getty Images
âPutin came to power in 1999,â Wolff wrote, after describing the fall of the Soviet Union and the subsequent âmoney grabâ in Russia. âControlling this new economy became his main political challenge.â
He continued, âWith great efficacy, he became, in effect, the chief banker and a significant equity holder in this parallel economy. Access to Putin was access to unregulated and unrestricted wealth. Putin was the regulator.â
Wolff said that since the mid-1990s, Trump, âexcluded from blue-chip financial sources, made continual efforts, both successful and not, to get a piece of the Putin action.â
âBeing a president is nice, but being an oligarch is forever,â he wrote.
Trump has been pursuing Putin since the mid-1990s, Wolff wrote.
âThe presidency has certainly given him access to other irregular financial opportunities, but Trump is a creature of habit, and no opportunity has loomed as large in his mind as the money he might make in a partnership of equals with Vladimir Putin. And even not so equal,â he concluded.
Reached for comment, White House spokesperson Davis Ingle told the Daily Beast in a frequently recycled statement: âMichael Wolff is a professional scumbag and serial liar whose brain has been completely warped by his severe and incurable disease known as Trump Derangement Syndrome.â

U.S. stock futures rose slightly on Monday night, following a mostly higher session on Wall Street as investors jumped back into tech names after a fierce sell-off last week.
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures traded 56 points higher, or 0.1%. S&P 500 futures climbed 0.1% along with Nasdaq-100 futures .
The S&P 500 climbed 0.4% in regular trading, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced more than 1%, with tech leading the charge. Nvidia added 1.4%, and Tesla jumped 3.8%. Alphabet shares advanced about 1%.
Tech last week suffered a rout that spilled over into the broader market, as concerns grew around companies borrowing too much money for their artificial intelligence build-outs.
"Improving moods regarding the prospects of modern technology have Wall Street breathing a sigh of relief as participants drop hedges, after the cost of volatility protection soared intraday on Friday, ahead of the intensifying selloff," wrote Jose Torres, senior economist at Interactive Brokers.
CoreWeave , which fell more than 25% last week, tried to recover some of that decline after a Goldman Sachs upgrade to buy. However, early gains fizzled and the stock closed slightly lower.
Investors on Tuesday will parse through a slew of corporate earnings. United Airlines is due to post after the bell, while General Motors is set to report before the open.
It's a busy week of earnings, with roughly 70 S&P 500 companies on deck to report results. Housing starts and pending home sales figures are also scheduled for release Tuesday.
AI stocks rallied on Monday, but CoreWeave closed slightly lower as investors remained skittish about its debt. Yields on Oracle debt also remained elevated as credit worries persist across the AI trade.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite gained 1% on Monday. CoreWeave , the so-called neocloud company that led the sell-off last week, bounced around, hit a 52-week low and ultimately closed fractionally lower. Meanwhile, its bond yields remained high and its five-year credit default swaps were at distressed levels.
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures traded 56 points higher, or 0.1%. S&P 500 futures climbed 0.1%. Nasdaq-100 futures advanced 0.2%.

articles.title_orig: Xbox Series X will offer identical graphics to the base PS5 in Grand Theft Auto VI
articles.title_zh: Xbox Series X will offer identical graphics to the base PS5 in Grand Theft Auto VI
articles.content_orig:
Social media is buzzing about user XGREEN's claim that the Xbox Series X console will offer a better price-to-performance ratio in the action game Grand Theft Auto VI than the PlayStation 5. However, current market data for 2026 and the technical aspects of multiplatform development completely refute this claim. Following Sony's global increase in recommended retail prices in April 2026 and Microsoft's counter-move in August 2026, the balance of power in the hardware market has shifted significantly. Due to a shortage of semiconductor components and a sharp rise in the cost of memory chips amid the AI ​​data center boom, the American corporation has significantly increased the price of its devices compared to its Japanese competitor. As a result, the base version of the PlayStation 5 Slim with a disc drive and a 1 TB storage drive is now officially priced at $649.99, while the PlayStation 5 Slim Digital costs $599.99. Meanwhile, the flagship Xbox Series X with a disc drive has increased in price to $799.99, its disc-less version, the Xbox Series X Digital, costs $749.99, and the entry-level Xbox Series S models with 512 GB and 1 TB of storage cost $499.99 and $599.99, respectively. This makes Sony's base console with a disc drive $150 cheaper than its direct competitor, Microsoft.
When it comes to visuals and performance in Grand Theft Auto VI, there won't be any noticeable difference in graphics quality, draw distance, or texture detail between the standard PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X. On paper, Microsoft's console does boast a more powerful graphics chip with full support for the AMD RDNA 2.0 architecture, which includes 52 compute units (CUs) clocked at 1.825 GHz and delivers 12.15 teraflops, compared to 36 CUs clocked at up to 2.23 GHz and 10.28 teraflops in the base PlayStation 5. Furthermore, the eight-core Zen 2 processor in the Xbox Series X runs at up to 3.8 GHz, compared to 3.5 GHz in its competitor, and a dedicated 10 GB of GDDR6 memory (out of a total of 16 GB) delivers 560 GB/s of bandwidth, compared to 448 GB/s on the Sony system. However, Rockstar Games builds its projects to a single technical standard for base consoles of the same generation, using identical graphics and asset settings at 30 frames per second, and the 18% difference in computing power is compensated for by dynamic resolution algorithms.
To date, Rockstar Games has exclusively showcased official footage from the PlayStation 5 console and hasn't released a single frame from Microsoft platforms. If players demand true technical superiority and maximum image quality in the upcoming release, the most powerful solution on the market is the enhanced PlayStation 5 Pro console with a 2 TB drive for $899.99, which outperforms both base systems in terms of hardware. The only significant advantage of the Xbox ecosystem remains the subscription service. Xbox Game Pass Ultimate, at $22.99 per month, includes access to in-house releases on day one, while PlayStation Plus, at $10.99–$19.99 per month, doesn't include new exclusives immediately upon release.

Apple’s new HomeView device was the center of the show at its smart home event on Tuesday, but the company also refreshed its HomePod mini smart speaker with a new chip and Siri AI integration, the latter of which will be available through a future update.
The $149 update is $50 more expensive than the original version launched over six years ago in 2020 . The new HomePod mini has an S10 chip that helps improve optimize dynamic range, loudness, and acoustic performance.
With the new HomePod mini, users can control their smart home devices through voice commands. Plus, the speaker can listen for sounds like a smoke alarm and send a notification to users’ phones — a feature that Alexa devices have offered for years.
Apple said that with Siri AI, users will be able to have multi-turn conversations, but it didn’t provide a date for when the new assistant will be available to HomePod mini 2 buyers.
The company also said the new speaker works better with its other devices. For instance, users could form a four-speaker home entertainment system paired with the new Apple TV 4K . Plus, the HomePod mini 2 speakers can be the default speaker for Mac for video calls or music playback instead of built-in speakers.
The device has another new feature, as well: a visual canvas called “Sound Glow,” which uses the color scheme of the album art to turn the top of the HomePod mini into a visual canvas that will glow and pulse in sync with the music. Users can also pick soundscapes like rain or ocean waves to start animations.
The new speaker comes in pink, green, blue, white, and midnight colorways and will be available starting October 30. Consumers can preorder starting today.

articles.title_orig: Deadly fire at Canada military base moved a kilometre 'in 30 to 60 seconds'
articles.title_zh: Deadly fire at Canada military base moved a kilometre 'in 30 to 60 seconds'
articles.content_orig:
WAINWRIGHT, Alberta — Fifty investigators are examining a fire at a Canadian military base that killed four soldiers and injured 39 others, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Monday, as questions mount over why training continued despite officials knowing a fire was burning nearby.
Speaking in Parliament in Ottawa, Carney said the Canadian Forces National Investigation Service was leading the investigation, with support from the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, into Saturday’s tragedy at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta.
Lawmakers observed a moment of silence before Carney addressed the House of Commons. Opposition party leaders also paid tribute.
“A fire was burning in the training area. Driven by ferocious winds, the fire jumped nearly a kilometer in less than a minute to where soldiers were gathered,” Carney said.
He said investigators had not determined what ignited the grass fire.
“We will get the answers to what caused this terrible tragedy, as expeditiously and transparently as necessary,” Carney later told reporters.
The fire overtook soldiers from the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia’s Canadian Light Infantry, and Army reservists conducting live-fire training.
Nineteen of the injured were in critical condition as of Monday. Conservative opposition leader Pierre Poilievre, who represents Wainwright in Parliament and was visiting the town, said many suffered severe burns requiring weeks or months of intensive care. He warned that their lives might never be the same.
Maj. Gen. Wade Rutland said Sunday that military officials knew about the fire for hours but believed it was contained and allowed training to continue before winds suddenly shifted.
About 84 soldiers from Charlie Company were training at two locations, one for throwing grenades and another for practicing attacks on simulated enemy positions. The fire swept into the second area.
Carney said the soldiers were preparing for a mission next spring to reinforce Canadian troops serving with NATO in Latvia.
Rutland said investigators would examine whether winds drove the flames toward the soldiers or whether the fire spread unseen through vegetation. They will also examine whether military safety procedures need to change.
The military identified those killed as Sgt. Morgan Wong of Edmonton; Pvt. Shaun Farrell of Prince Albert, Saskatchewan; Pvt. Aidan Goulding of North Vancouver, British Columbia; and Pvt. Hayden Lykkemark of Langley, British Columbia.
Carney remembered Goulding as someone who willingly took on difficult challenges, and Wong as someone his family could always depend on. He said Farrell and Lykkemark were best friends and that Lykkemark had dreamed of a career in law enforcement.
Poilievre recalled meeting Goulding during Canada Day celebrations at the base in July, when a group of young soldiers approached him for a photograph. After Saturday’s tragedy, someone sent him the picture identifying Goulding as one of those killed.
Poilievre also said he had heard accounts of soldiers who ran toward the flames to help their comrades, describing their actions as extraordinary acts of courage.
Military liaison officers were assisting families at hospitals in Edmonton, Calgary, Red Deer and Wainwright. Mental health teams and chaplains were also supporting soldiers and their families.
Carney ordered flags lowered to half-staff on all federal buildings nationwide Sunday in honor of the four soldiers killed.
Flowers were placed at Wainwright’s century-old war memorial, a stone clock tower honoring soldiers killed in past conflicts. The tower survived a devastating fire that swept through downtown Wainwright in 1929.
“They were training to defend Canada. To serve Canada. Now, Canada serves them,” Carney said.
Gillies reported from Edmonton, Alberta.

articles.title_orig: US adds ‘wrongful detention’ warning for Americans travelling to China
articles.title_zh: US adds ‘wrongful detention’ warning for Americans travelling to China
articles.content_orig:
US State Department is updating its travel advisory to alert Americans of the risk of being detained arbitrarily under Chinese law
The US State Department has added a “wrongful detention” warning to its travel advisory for China, alerting Americans to the risk of being detained arbitrarily under Chinese law.
On Monday, the official China travel advisory added the “D” risk indicator for wrongful detention, while maintaining the country’s overall advisory level at Level 2, or “Exercise Increased Caution”.
The advisory urges Americans travelling to mainland China to exercise caution due to the “arbitrary enforcement of local laws, the use of exit bans without a fair and transparent process under the law, and the risk of wrongful detention”.
The move comes as Washington and Beijing seek to maintain an improving bilateral relationship following a warm welcome for Chinese President Xi Jinping by US President Donald Trump during the September visit to Washington. The two leaders are expected to meet twice more this year.

articles.title_orig: Blue and White’s Benny Gantz pulls out of race, sealing precipitous political fall
articles.title_zh: Blue and White’s Benny Gantz pulls out of race, sealing precipitous political fall
articles.content_orig:
Benny Gantz withdraws from Israel's election race in bid to unseat Netanyahu
Benny Gantz, a former Israeli army chief and defence minister, has withdrawn from Israel’s election race after polls showed his party falling short of the threshold for entering parliament.
The leader of the Blue and White (Kahol Lavan) party announced on Monday he will not run in the October 27 polls, saying he will “continue to work for unity”.
The 67-year-old is expected to hold a news conference later on Monday.
Opinion polls in the lead-up to next week’s vote had consistently shown Gantz’s party hovering below the 3.25 percent threshold needed to enter the 120-seat Knesset, or Israel’s parliament.
A former main opposition leader, Gantz sat in a national unity government with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from 2020 to 2021.
He also joined Netanyahu’s war cabinet that was formed to oversee Israel’s genocidal war against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip after the Hamas-led attacks in southern Israel on October 7, 2023. Gantz quit the emergency cabinet in early June 2024, saying Netanyahu “is preventing us from advancing toward true victory”.
Reporting from Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh said Gantz’s election withdrawal announcement “was not really expected”, but added that many would see it as being “in line with how he’s conducted himself” after entering politics in 2018.
“This is a man who entered into unity governments with leaders – especially Netanyahu – that he expressly opposed,” said Odeh.
Gantz’s message for unity is narrow, Odeh added, as it referred to “a unity government of Zionist parties, so no Palestinian Israeli parties , no non-Zionist parties in the government, even if that means bringing in Netanyahu again”.
Netanyahu’s Likud party and the far-right coalition it leads is locked in a tight race with a self-styled Zionist opposition alliance heading into the election, according to recent polling, although neither side appears on track to win a parliamentary majority.
Two Arab-led electoral lists representing the Palestinian citizens of Israel, who make up about 20 percent of the population, are projected to win 13 seats and could be critical to any post-election coalition – but both main blocs have ruled out forming a government with them.
Opposition leaders, including Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot, who is seen as a potential prime minister candidate, welcomed Gantz’s decision as “correct” and “responsible”.
Alon Pinkas, a former Israeli ambassador and consul general in New York, told Al Jazeera Gantz’s exit from the race does not change the playing field as he was not going to have a major impact on the election.
“Electorally, his departure from the political system is completely irrelevant and inconsequential,” he said. “In terms of the politics, it is also inconsequential,” adding that Gantz had lost “a lot of his aura” when he “overstayed his welcome in the Netanyahu government”.

articles.title_orig: United Airlines adds 5 nonstop routes to its lineup — including new international destinations
articles.title_zh: United Airlines adds 5 nonstop routes to its lineup — including new international destinations
articles.content_orig:
United Airlines is adding a few new destinations to its friendly skies roster.
The airline announced this week that it will add five new nonstop North American routes, with three serving cities north of the border.
Of the new routes, three will be international expansions, and two will be domestic.
Experts say the domestic routes between Houston, TX and Joplin, MO, and between Washington Dulles and Lancaster, PA, stem from ongoing construction and subsequent operational restrictions at Chicago O’Hare International.
Meanwhile, the international additions of Denver to Ottawa, Denver to Quebec City, and Newark to St. John’s reflect the recent transborder business agreement between United and Air Canada.
Some of these Canadian routes are a welcome return while others mark the establishment of a completely new connection.
The Denver-to-Ottawa service re-establishes a former United Airlines route discontinued in 2010, alongside a fresh link between Denver and Quebec City.
Additionally, United will return to Newfoundland and Labrador for the first time since 2016 with seasonal flights connecting Newark and St. John’s.
Domestic service will begin this spring while the Canadian connections take flight this summer.
Meanwhile, to complement these additions, Air Canada is offering new connections between Toronto and Louisville and Quebec and Indianapolis, with seasonal service expected to run June through September of next year.
Air Canada is also taking off with new flights between Edmonton and Newark.
According to Bloomberg, United and Air Canada are looking to add as many as 10 additional US-Canada itineraries
“Air Canada and United’s long-standing partnership continues to deliver meaningful results for our customers and communities. For nearly three decades, Air Canada and United have worked to facilitate seamless travel and strengthen connectivity between Canada and the United States,” said Mark Galardo, Executive Vice President & Chief Commercial Officer and President, Cargo at Air Canada, on October 16 .
The added routes come amid a slew of other switches United Airlines has made of late.
Earlier this month, United launched a cheaper first-class fare .
Back in February, United quietly updated a noise policy that — before the change — had flyers nearly losing their minds .
The 100-year-old company told The Post it has started forcing passengers to wear headphones when listening to content on phones, tablets or anything that makes sound.
United’s Contract of Carriage — a rules and policy handbook — was updated on February 27 to add the new “headphone language.”
More recently, the “friendliness” of United’s skies was put in peril when a Russian woman was accused of biting and kicking  United flight attendants during a booze-fueled midair meltdown.

articles.title_orig: Apple Says iPhone Duo Not Available on Walk-In Basis in Two Countries
articles.title_zh: Apple Says iPhone Duo Not Available on Walk-In Basis in Two Countries
articles.content_orig:
For a limited time, the iPhone Duo and the iPhone 18 Pro Max will be limited to customers with a pickup reservation at Apple Stores in Japan and South Korea , according to notices posted on Apple's localized websites for those countries.
The notices suggest that the iPhone Duo will not be available for walk-in customers at Apple's retail locations in Japan and South Korea when the device launches on Friday, October 23, likely due to a mix of supply constraints and Apple's usual anti-scalping measures in Asia. It is unclear if this policy will extend to any other countries.
iPhone Duo pre-orders began on Friday , with shipping estimates on Apple's online store for newly-placed orders getting pushed back to January 25 within the first 30 minutes of pre-orders starting. In a statement issued later on Friday, Apple said demand for the iPhone Duo was " nothing short of extraordinary " and that it was "working hard" to fulfill orders "as quickly as possible." Apple did not disclose any specific sales figures.
Apple's online store says customers interested in reserving the iPhone Duo for Apple Store pickup should check back on Saturday, October 24 for more information.
iPhone Duo should be on display at Apple Stores around the world starting on Friday, October 23, but it is still not entirely clear if the device will be available for walk-in customers in the U.S. or any other countries, excluding Japan and South Korea. Our own Hartley Charlton reported that some Apple Store managers advised employees to warn customers against attempting to purchase the iPhone Duo on a walk-in basis at launch, but this was not companywide communication and Apple has yet to publicly comment on the matter.
It seems safe to say that even if some Apple Stores do have the iPhone Duo available for walk-in customers, inventory will be extremely limited at first.

articles.title_orig: Toyota’s best-selling Corolla is going electric, and it will be made in China
articles.title_zh: Toyota’s best-selling Corolla is going electric, and it will be made in China
articles.content_orig:
Toyota will produce the Corolla EV in China starting in 2028, alongside hybrid and gas-powered versions.
Since it went on sale in 1966, Toyota has sold over 57 million Corollas worldwide, making it the brand’s best-selling vehicle of all time.
Like the Prius, Toyota’s compact car attracted drivers with an affordable price and reputation as a reliable daily driver.
After 12 model changes, the next-generation Toyota Corolla is set for its biggest transformation to date.
Toyota revealed the next-gen Corolla Concept for the first time at the Japan Mobility Show almost a year ago. In addition to a pure electric version, former president and current CEO Koji Sato said the compact car would remain “a car for everyone,” with multiple powertrain options, including hybrid and gas-powered.
“Whether it’s a battery EV, plug-in hybrid, hybrid, or internal combustion engine vehicle―whatever the power source―let’s make good-looking cars that everyone will want to drive!” Toyota’s CEO said at the time.
According to Nikkei, Toyota plans to begin production of the next-gen Corolla in 2028 through its joint venture with Chinese state-owned FAW Group, FAW Toyota Motor.
The new Corolla will be the first to use Toyota’s “multipathway” platform that will support electric, hybrid, gas, and other powertrain options.
Toyota already uses the platform for several models, including under its luxury Lexus brand. By building the new Corolla in China, Toyota is expected to cut costs while speeding up development and output.
In addition to new longer-range electric vehicles, Toyota plans to build extended-range EVs under Lexus in China starting next year.
Toyota has yet to reveal any battery, powertrain specs, or other details. The next-gen Corolla is expected to remain close to the concept with a sleek, almost sports-car-like design. Aside from the huge COROLLA badge on the rear, you can barely tell it’s a Corolla.
In an exclusive interview with Japanese media NHK in July, Toyota’s current chairman and former CEO, Akio Toyoda, warned that the company is being forced to adapt, or “it cannot survive,” amid new competition and technology from China.
The special broadcast went behind the scenes at the “top secret” next-gen Corolla development site.
During the broadcast, several Corolla Concept body types , including a sedan, hatchback, crossover, and GR model, were shown blurred in the background.
The Toyota Corolla EV is expected to be available in single- and dual-motor configurations with a driving range of at least 250 miles.
The hybrid will reportedly use a new 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine and an electric motor. Toyota’s engineers told Car and Driver the system would deliver around 134 horsepower. It’s also estimated to be 10% to 20% more efficient than the current Corolla.
Whether or not Toyota will bring the Corolla EV to the US is still unclear. Toyota’s next-gen Corolla is expected to debut sometime in 2027 as a 2028 model year.
According to Car and Driver , the gas version will likely start at around $25,000, the hybrid around $27,000, and the EV and PHEVs will likely be priced in the $30,000 range.
While the Corolla is still a top seller, it has lost some of its charm as newer vehicles arrive that are more advanced, more efficient, and better looking.
It’s about time for an overhaul. In China, Toyota’s sales dropped by 23%, marking the seventh straight month of lower sales due to weak demand for gas and hybrid models amid soaring fuel prices.
Toyota is restructuring its two joint ventures , FAW Toyota and GAC Toyota, to streamline operations and introduce more advanced tech in China.

articles.title_orig: Rubio pitches US business in Central Asia, says China ties need not suffer
articles.title_zh: Rubio pitches US business in Central Asia, says China ties need not suffer
articles.content_orig:
Washington and five Central Asian nations outline plans for cooperation on minerals, transport and technology during Rubio’s Uzbek visit
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday that Washington wanted to compete for business in Central Asia without asking countries to stop working with China, as the United States and five regional governments outlined proposals to deepen cooperation on minerals, transport and technology.
Speaking in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, Rubio was asked what Washington could offer as Beijing expanded its presence in the region.
“I mean, look, it’s competition, right? We have products, we have companies; they make things. And we just want fair competition and an opportunity,” he said.
“This is not about coming here to say, ‘Stop talking to somebody else or stop working with some other country.’”
